question.question:
A firm pays dividends quarterly; the dividend just paid was 0.65 USD per share. The firm has 25 million shares outstanding. Stage one lasts 11 quarters; each quarterly dividend is -125 basis points higher than the previous one (one basis point is 0.01 percent; a negative figure is a cut), so the quarter-1 dividend already includes one quarter of growth. After stage one, dividends grow at 1 percent per year forever, converted to a quarterly growth rate by the nominal convention: 'compound' takes the rate that compounds over four quarters to the annual rate, 'nominal' divides the annual percentage by four. The required return is an effective annual rate of 5.5 percent; convert it to the equivalent compounded quarterly rate and discount each quarterly dividend at that rate. The terminal value at the end of the last stage-one quarter equals the first stage-two dividend divided by the quarterly rate minus the quarterly stage-two growth; the valuation is undefined unless that growth is below the quarterly rate. Report the quarterly discount rate in percent, the present value of stage-one dividends, the terminal value at the end of stage one, and the share price today (stage-one present value plus discounted terminal value).

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd` with no unit label or additional text.
